name: Vitaliy Khomutynnik
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Cascade Investment Fund (Ukraine); President, Ukrainian Golf Federation
profile: Ukrainian entrepreneur and former MP (Verkhovna Rada 2002-2019) from Makiivka who founded Cascade in the 1990s and built holdings in gas production (Ukrnaftoburinnya, JKX Oil & Gas), insurance and agriculture (Kernel stake, Cascade-Agro). Between 2020 and 2023 he exited oil, gas and farmland, and he now runs Cascade as an investor in VC funds, European tech and Kyiv real estate (Respublika Park mall).
interesting_fact: He has pivoted from gas to tech. Cascade sold its JKX Oil & Gas, Ukrnaftoburinnya, Kernel and Cascade-Agro stakes (2020-23) and now invests via Cascade Ventures in funds and startups such as Wefox, McMakler and Discord.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000, at age 24, he served as 'Minister of Fuel and Energy' in Ukraine's Youth Government, years before he owned gas-production assets. He later backed mobile-game startup Playco, which was valued at about $1bn in 2020.
notes: Former Party of Regions/Opposition Bloc MP, often described in the press as an oligarch. He was sanctioned by Russia in 2018 and reportedly lives abroad. I found no published contact for Cascade Investment Fund. cascadeventures.com looks like an unrelated company, so don't use it. Energy angle: a gas-to-venture pivot.

name: Lord Alliance
profile: David Alliance, Baron Alliance (born 1932, Kashan, Iran) was a Lib Dem peer, founding shareholder and former chairman of mail-order group N Brown, and co-founder of textiles group Coats Viyella. He died on 18 July 2025, aged 93.
notes: Died 18 July 2025 (N Brown announcement, reported by FashionUnited and The JC). Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Terry Smith
profile: Terry Smith (born 1953, East London) is a former top-rated bank analyst who ran broker Collins Stewart and then Tullett Prebon. In 2010 he founded Fundsmith, whose buy-good-companies-and-do-nothing equity fund is one of the UK's largest (about £24bn under management). He is often called 'the English Warren Buffett'.
interesting_fact: His 1992 book 'Accounting for Growth', which exposed creative accounting at FTSE 100 firms, got him fired and sued by UBS Phillips & Drew. The row sent the book to No. 1, displacing Stephen Hawking's 'A Brief History of Time'.
deep_cut_fact: A military-history enthusiast, he led the campaign that put a statue of Battle of Britain commander Sir Keith Park in London. He was made a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit (2012) for services to NZ-UK relations. He also cycles competitively and practises Muay Thai.

public_contacts.value: Press contact: Charlotte Balbirnie, 07989 528421 (as published on Fundsmith site)

notes: Very media-friendly. He writes an annual shareholder letter and hosts an annual shareholder meeting that is posted on Fundsmith's YouTube channel. The best route is the Fundsmith press contact.

name: Liu Haifeng
current_role: Executive Chairman and co-founder, DCP Capital (德弘资本)
profile: Liu Haifeng (David H. Liu) is a veteran China private-equity investor. He co-headed Morgan Stanley Private Equity Asia, then was a KKR partner, co-head of KKR Asia PE and CEO of KKR Greater China. In 2017 he left with Julian Wolhardt to co-found DCP Capital, a China-focused PE firm. His deals include Mengniu Dairy, Ping An, Haier, Belle and Nanfu Battery.
interesting_fact: He was KKR's first local hire in Asia, and he backed some of China's best-known private-equity deals, including Mengniu Dairy and Ping An Insurance.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer. He graduated as Class Salutatorian from Columbia with a B.S. in Electrical Engineering, was a Tau Beta Pi member, and won the Edwin Howard Armstrong Memorial Award for Columbia's top electrical engineering student.
notes: Uses the English name David H. Liu. A low-profile PE investor. The best route is DCP Capital's general inbox (info@dcpcapital.com). The site also has a Charity section.

name: Sun Jie
current_role: CEO and Director, Trip.com Group (Nasdaq: TCOM; HKEX: 9961)
profile: Jane Jie Sun (孙洁) is the CEO of Trip.com Group (formerly Ctrip), one of the world's largest online travel companies. She was an audit manager at KPMG in Silicon Valley and then head of SEC reporting at Applied Materials. She joined Ctrip as CFO in 2005, became COO in 2012 and has been CEO since November 2016. She is also a director of iQIYI.
interesting_fact: She spent her pre-Ctrip career in Silicon Valley. After five years as a KPMG audit manager there, she ran the SEC and external reporting division at chip-equipment maker Applied Materials from 1997 to 2005.
deep_cut_fact: She did her first two undergraduate years at Peking University before finishing at the University of Florida's Fisher School of Accounting with high honors (1992). In 2010, already a Ctrip executive, she went back to Peking University Law School for an LL.M.
notes: Known in English as Jane Sun. She is a high-profile CEO who speaks often at travel-industry forums (Skift, PATA), which makes conference organisers or Trip.com corporate comms a plausible route. Trip.com press releases now date from Singapore. Data-center angle: Trip.com is a large-scale tech platform.

name: Qiu Shixun
current_role: Shareholder of Glodon Co., Ltd. (广联达, SZSE: 002410), per Hurun. I could not confirm a current role.
profile: Qiu Shixun (邱世勋) appears on the Hurun China Rich List (2020-2021) with his wealth attributed to Glodon, Beijing's leading construction-cost and BIM (building information modelling) software company, founded in 1998 and now led by chairman Yuan Zhenggang and founder Diao Zhizhong. I could not find an independent biography confirming his exact role (e.g. as an early co-founder or shareholder).
interesting_fact: Glodon, the source of his wealth, makes construction-cost estimating and BIM software. It is pushing 'industry AI' and digital-twin tools for engineering and construction, which is relevant to data-center and energy-infrastructure builds.
notes: Very low profile, with no English or Chinese bio found in web search. He is not in recent Glodon executive lists. The only route is via Glodon IR or the company. Verify his role with Glodon's prospectus or annual reports (cninfo) before outreach.

name: Xuan Ruiguo
current_role: Former actual controller and chairman of Guangdong Huatie Tongda High-speed Railway Equipment (*ST华铁, 000976, now delisted). I could not confirm a current title.
profile: Xuan Ruiguo (宣瑞国) built a rail-equipment business supplying China's high-speed train programme (Huatie Tongda) and earlier chaired Hong Kong-listed China Automation Group, a provider of safety and critical-control systems. He resigned from the Huatie board in 2024, and the company was later delisted. He appeared on the Hurun China list 2010-2020.
interesting_fact: Before the high-speed rail venture, he chaired China Automation Group, an industrial safety and critical-control systems company listed in Hong Kong.
notes: Caution: a 2024 SZSE disciplinary decision names him as actual controller and former chairman of Huatie Tongda, and the listed company has been delisted. He is a poor outreach candidate, and I found no published contacts.

name: Sun Ximin
current_role: Senior Chairman (资深董事长) and co-actual controller, Shandong Minhe Animal Husbandry Co. (民和股份, SZSE: 002234)
profile: Sun Ximin (孙希民) built Minhe, a Penglai, Shandong-based poultry group whose main product is commercial broiler chicks. He took it public on the Shenzhen exchange (002234) and has handed the chairmanship to his son Sun Xianfa while staying on as senior chairman and largest individual shareholder (about 47m shares, per the FY2025 report).
interesting_fact: Minhe runs a circular-agriculture energy business. Its subsidiary Minhe Biological (民和生物) turns manure from the group's chicken farms into biogas for grid power generation and upgraded bio-natural gas, plus organic fertiliser.
notes: Hurun pairs him with his son Sun Xianfa (now chairman). The biogas-to-power angle fits an energy podcast. The route is the board secretary's office, as published in the annual report. Low English-language profile. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so the profile comes from the filing only.

name: Zhangting
current_role: Shareholder of Sichuan Yahua Industrial Group (雅化集团, SZSE: 002497). As of 2017 she was its largest listed holder (31.9m shares). No executive role found.
profile: Zhang Ting (张婷) is listed by Hurun (2017) alongside Yahua's controlling shareholder and chairman Zheng Rong. Yahua's 2017 annual report names her as Zheng Rong's direct relative and its largest named shareholder. Yahua began as a civil-explosives and blasting group and has become a major battery-grade lithium hydroxide and carbonate producer. She is not among the directors or executives in the 2025 report.
interesting_fact: Yahua, the source of the family's wealth, has moved from mining explosives into battery lithium. It has about 130kt a year of lithium-salt capacity, supplies Tesla, LGES, SK On and CATL under major contracts, and targets EV and energy-storage markets.
notes: A passive shareholder with no public profile. The better podcast guest is probably chairman Zheng Rong (born 1953, started as a worker at Ya'an Chemical Plant in 1971 and rose to run it), reachable via Yahua's board office. Web search budget was exhausted, so this entry is based on the filings only.

name: Yang Yanliang
current_role: Chairman, Shandong Bohui Group (山东博汇集团), as of the 2017 filing. He is former chairman and actual controller of Shandong Bohui Paper (600966).
profile: Yang Yanliang (杨延良) built the Bohui group in Huantai, Zibo, Shandong, into a major paper and board maker (Bohui Paper, SSE: 600966) with chemicals (Shandong/Jiangsu Haili Chemical) and power assets. Bohui Paper is now indirectly controlled by APP's Gold East Paper (金光纸业), so his current holdings centre on the private Bohui Group. Hurun lists him with Li Xiurong.
interesting_fact: Besides paper, his 2017 roles included chairman of Shandong Tianyuan Thermal Power (山东天源热电) and of Shandong Kerun Investment, plus executive director of Jiangsu Haili Chemical. That is an industrial energy and chemicals side to a paper fortune.
notes: Bohui Paper's published IR email (zqb@bohui.com) now belongs to the APP-controlled listed company, not to him, so it is not a good route. I found no published contact for the private Bohui Group. Web search budget was exhausted, so check whether he is still active. Very low public profile.

name: Pan Xianwen
current_role: Founder and former chairman/actual controller of Chongqing Sansheng Industrial (三圣股份, SZSE: 002742, now 冀衡医药). Control passed to Xiao Hui and Xiao Qiusheng on 10 Dec 2025. No current role found.
profile: Pan Xianwen (潘先文, born 1963) is an engineer-entrepreneur from Chongqing. He ran the Jiangbei gypsum and special building-materials plants from 1995 and built Sansheng into a listed maker of concrete admixtures, expansion agents and building materials, which Hurun classes as 'green material'. He was a Chongqing People's Congress deputy, and control of the company changed hands in December 2025.
interesting_fact: He is a hands-on materials engineer with patents (e.g. an expansion-clinker and expansion-agent preparation method). He led development of products such as the PCA polycarboxylate superplasticiser and the 'U-type' concrete expansion agent.
deep_cut_fact: He helped develop and build China's first process and plant for making sulfuric acid from anhydrite (gypsum) while co-producing cement, and he co-authored technical papers on tunnel-kiln calcination of expansion clinker.
notes: He is no longer the controlling shareholder of the listed company (changed Dec 2025, per the FY2025 annual report: http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-03-31/1225057323.PDF), so the company IR (ir@cqssgf.com) is no longer a route to him. I found no personal or office contact. Web search budget was exhausted.

name: Gao Jinna
current_role: Former major shareholder of Lander Sports Development (莱茵体育, SZSE: 000558, now 天府文旅), acting in concert with Lander Holding Group. No current executive role found.
profile: Gao Jinna (高靖娜) is linked to Hangzhou's Lander (莱茵达) group, founded and chaired by Gao Jisheng, with whom Hurun lists her. In 2012 Lander Holding transferred 100m shares of the listed Lander company (a property developer that later pivoted to sports) to her. Lander Holding sold control to Chengdu Sports Investment Group in 2019, and the company is now Tianfu Cultural Tourism.
interesting_fact: The Lander listed vehicle she held shares in made one of China's more unusual pivots, from Hangzhou property developer to 'Lander Sports Development' (sports venues and events). After its 2019 sale to Chengdu's state sports-investment group it became Tianfu Cultural Tourism.
notes: Private, with no public profile. The listed company is now Chengdu-state-controlled, so its IR inbox is not a route to her. lander.com.cn did not respond. Any approach would go via Lander Holding Group (Hangzhou, chaired by Gao Jisheng), for which I found no published contact. Web search budget was exhausted.

name: Liu Qun
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Tiansheng Pharmaceutical Group (天圣制药, SZSE: 002872, trading as ST天圣)
profile: Liu Qun (刘群) founded Chongqing-based Tiansheng Pharmaceutical Group, a maker of infusions, injectables and solid-dose drugs that listed in Shenzhen in 2017, and he remains its controlling shareholder per the FY2025 annual report.
notes: Not recommended. Per the company's FY2025 annual report, a final 2024 Chongqing High Court ruling upheld his criminal conviction for embezzling and misappropriating company funds (since repaid), and the stock is under risk warning (ST). Source: http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-04-29/1225249815.PDF

name: Li Huoming
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jiangsu Chuanzhi Podcast Education Technology (传智教育 / Itcast, SZSE: 003032); also chairman of Xiamen Youyou Huilian Information Technology (since Mar 2025)
profile: Li Huoming (黎活明, born 1980) is a software engineer turned education entrepreneur. In 2009 he founded Beijing Chuanzhi Podcast (Itcast), which grew into the listed IT-skills trainer behind the 'Heima Programmer' (黑马程序员) in-person bootcamps and the 'Boxuegu' (博学谷) online platform. It now focuses on AI development, LLM, big-data and HarmonyOS courses.
interesting_fact: Itcast has repositioned itself as an AI-talent pipeline. Its courses now include AI large-model development (Python), AI big data, AI embedded/robotics and AI HarmonyOS development, run from teaching centres across major Chinese cities.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Itcast he worked as a senior software engineer at Beijing Lianhe Chuangke Telecom (2004) and as tech manager at China Agriculture Network (2003). His official bio lists Oct 2006 to Jun 2009 simply as 'writing' (写作), the period before he started Itcast in June 2009.
notes: Founder-CEO of a listed coding and AI-training company. An AI-talent and data-skills angle could interest him. The route is Itcast IR. Web search budget was exhausted, so the profile comes from the FY2025 annual report.

name: Li Mantie
current_role: Chairman and President, Shenzhen Ledman Optoelectronic Co. (雷曼光电, SZSE: 300162)
profile: Li Mantie (李漫铁, born 1968) is a radio engineer and senior engineer who founded Shenzhen Ledman Optoelectronic, an LED display maker now focused on COB-packaged Micro LED ultra-fine-pitch screens. He remains chairman and president and holds civic roles, including Guangdong CPPCC member, Nanshan District People's Congress deputy and SUSTech industry professor.
interesting_fact: He serves as a distinguished industry professor at Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) and as vice-chairman of the display-application branch of the China Optics and Optoelectronics Manufacturers Association.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in radio technology at South China University of Technology's radio engineering department. His first job was as a clerk on the Huizhou municipal government's Radio Management Committee, before he ran Huizhou Yuexin Communications Development and later founded Ledman.
notes: An active founder-chairman, with Micro LED display tech as the hook. The best route is Ledman's board secretary office. Web search budget was exhausted, so the profile comes from the FY2025 annual report.

name: Zhu Hongtao
current_role: Employee-representative Director, Joyoung Co. (九阳股份, SZSE: 002242), part of the JS Global Lifestyle group; executive director of several Shanghai investment companies
profile: Zhu Hongtao (朱宏韬, born 1970) is a long-time member of the Joyoung team, the Hangzhou kitchen-appliance maker best known for household soymilk makers, which sits within JS Global Lifestyle (HK-listed, former parent of SharkNinja). He previously chaired Joyoung's supervisory board and is now an employee-representative director. He also runs several Shanghai holding and investment vehicles.
interesting_fact: Joyoung builds the 'space kitchen' for China's space station. It has held the task since 2014, and its food-heating and drinking-water equipment went up with the Tianhe core module in April 2021 and has run for more than 1,500 days.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MBA from Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, an unusual credential among the founding-era Joyoung executives.
notes: Low public profile, and Hurun attributes his wealth to his JS Global Life stake. The route is Joyoung's board secretary office. The space-kitchen story is a good hook. Web search budget was exhausted, so the profile comes from the FY2025 annual report.
